name: Soca & Wining
notes: Soca & Wining style pack (Doc 04 template). Genuinely solo — carnival needs no partner, only a road. Lineage told straight: Trinidad & Tobago's carnival descends from emancipation celebrations (Canboulay) — a freed people's festival that colonial power tried to ban and the people kept; soca the music was created in the 1970s by Garfield Blackman — Lord Shorty, later Ras Shorty I — fusing calypso with East Indian rhythms (his own account: the 'soul of calypso'). Wining — the rolling hip rotation at the center of carnival dance — is Afro-Caribbean movement language, danced from Trinidad to the whole diaspora. CONSENT IS CURRICULUM: wining with someone at carnival or a fete is invited and answered — the culture's own etiquette, taught here as a first-class node. Design truths: the wine is hip isolation over released knees (gated like the shimmy); carnival is an endurance event (stamina gates are real); and the diaspora carnivals — Notting Hill, Brooklyn's Labor Day, Caribana — mean the road reaches almost everyone.

seasons.finale: Film yourself chipping to one full soca track — the carnival march, relaxed, endless.
Film the wine: slow circles both directions over soft knees — isolated, unhurried, yours.
Film figure-8 and standing wine variations riding a groovy soca track — control before speed.
Film 60 seconds of power soca energy — jump, wave, wine, chip — without the form collapsing.
Find the fete or the carnival — Trinidad if you can, the diaspora carnivals wherever you are. Play a mas or chip beside one.

attributes.name: Hip isolation L1
attributes.test: 20 slow hip circles each direction with the ribcage pinned still — the wine is hips alone

attributes.name: Knee release L1
attributes.test: 60s of soft bouncing knees, fully relaxed — the wine rides released knees, never locked ones

attributes.name: Road stamina L2
attributes.test: three soca tracks of continuous chip-and-wine — carnival is measured in hours, train in songs

nodes.name: Groovy and power — soca's two speeds
checkpoints: groovy soca rolls near 110-120 BPM — the wine's home; power soca charges at 155-165 — the jump-and-wave engine
the drums-and-iron 'engine room' drives everything; find the iron (the struck brake-drum ring) in any track
soca instructs from the mic — when the artist says jump, the road jumps; listening IS the dance

nodes.name: The road mix — pacing a carnival
checkpoints: a road day runs for hours: chip to conserve, wine on the grooves, explode for the power songs
the annual Road March race crowns the song the road loved most — learn each year's contenders
pace like the veterans: the best masqueraders finish the day still dancing

nodes.name: Emancipation's festival — Canboulay to carnival
checkpoints: Trinidad carnival descends from emancipation celebrations — Canboulay, the freed people's festival that colonial authorities tried to suppress (the 1881 Canboulay riots resisted the ban) and the people kept
J'ouvert's dawn mud-and-paint and the mas bands' costumes both carry that history of freedom claimed in the street
to play mas is to join a festival built by freed people — dance it knowing that

nodes.name: Lord Shorty — the man who made soca
checkpoints: soca was created in the 1970s by Garfield Blackman — Lord Shorty, later Ras Shorty I — fusing calypso with East Indian rhythms; he called it the 'soul of calypso'
calypso's lineage (and its own griot-like calypsonians) is the parent tradition — soca is its carnival-engine child
from Shorty to Machel Montano and today's Road March winners: one unbroken road

nodes.name: Consent on the road — wining etiquette
checkpoints: wining WITH someone is invited and answered — a look, an ask, a yes; carnival's own etiquette, not an import
'it's just carnival' never overrides somebody's no — the culture itself says so, loudly
your own wine needs nobody's permission; sharing it always does

nodes.name: The wine
checkpoints: hips roll in smooth circles over released knees — the ribcage floats still above
both directions, equally — the road doesn't care which way you started
slow control first: a slow wine with full isolation beats any fast blur
the raqs pack's hipwork and this move are cousins across an ocean — the isolation discipline transfers
mistakes: circling the whole torso instead of the hips
locked knees (nothing rolls on a stiff base)

nodes.name: Figure-8s & the standing wine
checkpoints: the circle becomes an eight — hips sweeping side to side through the middle
level changes: wine standing tall, wine sitting low (the low wine is earned by the knees)
add the arms: one hand up, phone in the air, flag out — carnival styling is joy made visible

nodes.name: The chip
checkpoints: the carnival march: a relaxed shuffling step-drag that travels miles without spending you
knees soft, feet barely leaving the road, shoulders easy
chip and wine together — the road's default state — should feel like resting
mistakes: marching it stiff (the chip is the laziest step you'll ever perfect)

nodes.name: Jump and wave (power soca)
checkpoints: when the power song drops: jump on the beat, wave the rag or flag, wine in the air if you can
land soft every jump — carnival knees are a marathon budget
burst and recover: power sections are sprints inside the road's marathon
mistakes: spending everything on the first power song (there are twelve more coming)

nodes.name: The road simulation — filmed
checkpoints: a three-track set: chip through a groovy opener, wine through the middle, jump-and-wave the power closer
the test is joy that survives fatigue — carnival's whole secret
film the last 30 seconds: if you're still smiling, you passed

nodes.name: The fete or the road
checkpoints: find soca live: a fete, a diaspora carnival (Notting Hill, Brooklyn Labor Day, Caribana, Miami), or Trinidad itself if the road ever calls you
consent etiquette in your pocket, stamina in your legs, Shorty's name in your mouth
notice what a street full of people wining in freedom actually is — that's Canboulay still going
